Questions

Solomon or Nathan

Which son of David, and where do the lines cross?

After David the lists part: Matthew follows the kings, Luke a son known only by name. They touch once more at Shealtiel and Zerubbabel.

Solomon or Nathan

After David, Matthew follows the kings through Solomon; Luke follows Nathan, a son of David known only by name. Luke’s line never passes through Jechoniah, on whom Jeremiah pronounced ‘childless’ for David’s throne.

Where they meet again

Both lines pass through Shealtiel and Zerubbabel, then diverge again. Matthew and 1 Chronicles 3:17 make Shealtiel Jechoniah’s son; Luke makes him Neri’s. 1 Chronicles 3:19 makes Zerubbabel son of Pedaiah, Shealtiel’s brother.

Numbers count from Adam as 1, following the critical Greek text, which reads Admin and Arni where the WEB has Aram (hence 27–28). Gold numbers fall on multiples of seven: Enoch 7, Abraham 21, David 35, Jesus 77.

In the tradition

Jechoniah · Jewish Rabbinic tradition holds that Jechoniah repented in prison and the decree was annulled, since Zerubbabel, his grandson, is called a signet ring in Haggai 2:23 (reversing Jer 22:24) (Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 24; Leviticus Rabbah 19:6; cf. b. Sanhedrin 37b–38a).

Nathan · Patristic Augustine at first read Luke’s line through Nathan as priestly, because Nathan the prophet brought David to repentance. He later corrected himself: the mystery lies ‘not in the same man but in the same name’ (Retractations 1.26 and 2.16, PL 32:627, 637).

Nathan · Scholarship Zechariah 12:12 sets ‘the house of Nathan’ beside ‘the house of David’ in the end-time mourning, which some take to show a Nathanite family with its own standing after the exile.
